sentence: This project builds germanium detectors and uses AI to improve how they detect low-energy particles and make medical imaging more accurate.
This project tests whether electrical measurements of red blood cells can show early changes caused by oxidative stress.
This project builds computer methods that learn from data stored as graphs and find unusual changes in that data.
This project builds a moving target defense to help power grids spot and recover from attacks that tamper with their data.
This project checks how accurate past forecasts of threatened wildlife populations were by comparing them with later monitoring data.
This project builds intelligent systems that watch human workers in manufacturing and give them real-time corrections to prevent mistakes.
This project studies how DNA nanotubes build themselves and how proteins in cell membranes work.
This project studies how a group of phage-plasmids that infect a marine bacterium differ from one another and what shapes those differences.
This project studies how sex chromosomes change over time by comparing several treehopper species whose sex chromosomes recently arose.
This project uses an electroencephalogram system that records the brain's electrical activity to study reward responses to faces and mild traumatic brain injuries.
This project builds mathematical tools that pull apart overlapping brain processes that run at different speeds, using brain recordings from mice.
This project sorts groundwater wells by the geologic formation they tap and estimates how much groundwater irrigated farms take out.
This project builds learning methods that keep working well as more data keeps arriving from many views, and that resist attacks meant to fool them.
This project studies whether market involvement, religious beliefs and social traits affect the local ecological knowledge of indigenous communities.
This project tries to find out how cells stop the cell cycle when ribosome biogenesis is blocked, by comparing yeast with Drosophila.
This project uses a portable Magnetic Resonance Imaging scanner to take brain images in schools and clinics for studies of cognition, behavior and health.
This project develops control methods that keep a soft robotic arm moving safely while it touches a person.
This project holds a workshop where experts discuss how to turn quantum sensors from lab demonstrations into tools that work in biomedical imaging.
This project studies how neurons and glia pass mitochondria to each other, and what triggers that transfer, using the fruit fly.
